summary: Security review focused on regional routing / geofencing, KMS options and cross-border processing. Novena wants strong assurance their EU patient data never leaves jurisdiction and clear visibility of subprocessors + audit logs. Discussed Redwood's region pinning, private KMS options, and tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated routing. Agreed next steps: send compliance artifacts, share KMS guide, schedule EU-only pilot.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we appreciate you taking the time.
[00:06] Elena Kovač: Thanks, Maya. Quick background: Novena handles EU clinical trial data, so our default is EU residency and minimal cross-border processing. We're here to validate Redwood's controls for that.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Got it. We'll walk through region pinning, KMS choices, and subprocessor responsibilities. Happy to dive deep where you want.
[00:26] Tomás Rivera: I have a couple specific requrements — no outbound egress to US for EU-tagged datasets, and audit trails that show which region handled inference.
[00:38] Lin Zhao: For region pinning we support policy-level routing — you can tag requests with region=eu and we route to EU-only clusters. If a region is unhealthy we can fail closed or fallback to a pre-approved secondary region, but that'll be a policy choice.
[00:53] Elena Kovač: Fail closed is prefered, we can't allow fallback to US without a legal review.
[00:58] Maya Chen: That's fine. We have a policy option \"strict region\" that returns an error instead of falling back. We can document the SLO tradeoffs.
[01:07] Tomás Rivera: How do we get telemetry to prove inference execution location? We need logs that show region, node id, and timestamps for audit.
[01:16] Samir Patel: We emit per-request metadata in audit logs: region tag, model variant, node id and request id. Logs can be pushed to your SIEM via secure delivery or stored in our audit retention. Be aware retention tiers vary.
[01:29] Alex Gran: Can we get log delivery to our Splunk instance?
[01:32] Samir Patel: Yes, we support syslog/S3 push. We'll share the exact endpoints.
[01:36] Priya Menon: On subprocessors — we need a full list of any third parties that process data in EU and a contractual commitment about cross-border transfers.
[01:45] Maya Chen: We'll share our subprocessor inventory. For hosted we use several infra subprocessors; for Private/dedicated we can reduce that surface and provide a tighter list.
[01:54] Elena: What's the difference between dedicated and private in terms of subprocessors?
[01:59] Lin Zhao: Dedicated means reserved GPU pools in our infra but still managed by Redwood; subprocessors are similar to hosted but we can isolate networking. Private (VPC/on-prem) reduces Redwood-managed subprocessors because you control networking and storage.
[02:12] Tomás: Ok. KMS — we need to ensure keys for EU data never leave EU, ideally customer-managed keys in a KMS we control. What options do you offer?
[02:23] Samir: We support three patterns: Redwood-managed KMS (default), Customer-managed KMS via cloud KMS (you give us a key or we use an IAM-binding), and a hybrid where keys are escrowed with a trusted custodian. For strict residency we recommend customer-managed keys hosted in an EU KMS with tenant-limited key usage.
[02:41] Elena: If we provide CMK in Azure Key Vault (EU region), can Redwood use it without the key material leaving the region?
[02:48] Lin: Yes — we integrate via standard KMS keywrap modes. The key material stays with your cloud provider; Redwood receives wrapped keys or uses envelope encryption and never sees raw key material. We'll need appropriate IAM permissions and a small setup.
[03:02] Tomás: How about HSM-backed keys and key rotation?
[03:05] Samir: Supported. Rotation is driven on your side; Redwood will re-encrypt model caches or KV store objects as needed. We'll include rotation guidance in the doc.
[03:13] Elena: Are there any subprocessors in the EU we should be aware of?
[03:17] Maya: We have EU datacenter partners (compute) and a monitoring vendor. We'll include names in the inventory.
[03:22] Priya: We need contract language to prevent subprocessor changes without notice and a right to object.
[03:27] Maya: Standard — 30 day notice and objection window is our typical approach; we can put that in the DPA.
[03:32] Tomás: What about telemetry — do you redact PII from logs by default?
[03:36] Lin: Default is structured logs with request IDs and metadata. Payload content is not logged unless you opt-in. We can configure PII redaction rules.
[03:45] Elena: On SOC 2 and ISO — can you share audit reports?
[03:49] Maya: Yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certs are shareable under an NDA; we'll send the redacted reports.
[03:56] Priya: We require proof of SOC 2 for our procurement. Also need a mapping of controls to our questionnaire.
[04:03] Samir: We'll provide a controls matrix mapping to common frameworks — we'll include the specific mappings you requested.
[04:09] Tomás: One more technical: if we tag a dataset as EU-only and then call embeddings then the vector store — does that stay in EU, or could an embedding job call an external API?
[04:19] Lin: All inference work for EU-tagged requests remains in EU clusters and any helper services are also EU-located for that tenant. If you integrate third-party tools we call out the behavior.
[04:29] Alex: For the pilot we'd like to run a single model with synthetic staging data routed to EU, and validate logs and KMS usage. How long to spin that up?
[04:36] Maya: We can provision an EU-only trial within 72 hours once we have your staging creds and IP allowlist.
[04:41] Tomás: Good. Can we get SLA wording about region enforcement?
[04:45] Maya: We can add a contractual exhibit that states region enforcement policy and remedies for breach — likely an SLA credit or termination right depending on severity. Legal will need to discuss details.
[04:55] Priya: Please note we also have regulatory reporting obligations; we may need logs with chain-of-custody for 7 years. What's Redwood retention max?
[05:05] Samir: Our audit log tiers go up to 7 years as an add-on. For hosted defaults it's shorter. We'll include retention tiers and pricing.
[05:14] Elena: Any risks where data could be mirrored for backups outside EU?
[05:18] Lin: Backups respect region policy; for EU-only tenancy we restrict backups to EU replicas unless you authorize cross-border replication.
[05:27] Tomás: About fallbacks again — is there a way to configure an emergency manual override with approvals?
[05:32] Maya: Yes, an admin-level override procedure that requires SSO-authenticated approval and audit trail. We can detail that in runbook.
[05:40] Priya: On SSO and RBAC integration — we use SAML with SCIM for provisioning. How mature is Redwood's SSO?
[05:47] Samir: We support SAML2.0, OIDC and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is hierarchical — org, project, route-level. We'll share a sample SCIM configuration and the default roles.
[05:58] Elena: Do keys get rotated when a user is deprovisioned?
[06:02] Lin: Key rotation is independent of SSO deprovisioning. We recommend a regular rotation cadence and revoking keys for compromised tenants; we can automate some workflows but customer-managed keys remain under your control.
[06:12] Tomás: Any encryption in transit specifics?
[06:14] Samir: TLS 1.2+ with forward secrecy; we also support mutual TLS for private links.
[06:20] Maya: Quick check — are there any blockers for Novena to proceed with a pilot?
[06:25] Elena: Main blockers are legal signoff on DPA and confirmation that KMS customer-managed keeps keys within EU.
[06:31] Priya: And we need the subprocessor list.
[06:34] Maya: We'll get those over. Samir, can you take point on KMS doc?
[06:38] Samir: Yep, I'll share the integration guide and an example terraform snippet for Azure Key Vault.
[06:44] Tomás: Would love a short runbook for incident flow if a region fails.
[06:48] Lin: We'll include an incident runbook with escalation matrix.
[06:52] Maya: Great. We'll recap next steps and target dates. Thanks all.
[06:57] Elena: Thanks everyone.
closing_recap: Recap: Redwood to provide SOC2/ISO docs, subprocessor inventory, KMS integration guide, and an incident runbook. Novena to provide staging creds/IP allowlist for EU-only pilot. Agreed: pilot provisioning ~72 hours after staging details provided. Next meeting: pilot kickoff to be scheduled after artifacts are shared.
